expected_evidence: Sedimentary layers (the Younger Dryas Boundary 'black mat') with anomalous magnetic and carbon microspherule concentrations across multiple North American sites
Nanodiamonds, lonsdaleite, and platinum-group element (Pt/Ir) anomalies co-located with the microspherule layer
Peer-reviewed geochemical/stratigraphic reports and their disputes (e.g., Firestone et al. 2007 vs. Pigati et al. 2012, Daulton et al., Surovell et al.) as model-prior literature
Archaeological correlation with Clovis-age occupation horizons directly beneath the layer, showing cultural/faunal discontinuity
Megafaunal bone assemblages showing an extinction pulse timed to the layer
Search results, positive or negative, for an associated impact crater or airburst structure in North America or Greenland
Independent replication studies testing whether the spherule layer is a synchronous continent-wide/global event or locally reworked material
Ice-core or varve records near 12,800 cal BP showing an ash/dust/soot spike consistent with impact fallout
response.rationale: This corresponds to the Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis (model-prior, unverified from training knowledge), so the relevant period is best treated as 'younger-dryas' rather than unspecified. The primary claimed evidence is geological (microspherule/nanodiamond/PGE layers), with moderate-high detectability (0.65) since terminal-Pleistocene sediment sequences and black-mat horizons are well preserved and have been sampled at many sites. Material/archaeological correlation has lower detectability (0.35) given sparse, disturbed Clovis-age sites. Astronomical evidence (a crater or airburst structure) has decent theoretical detectability (0.7) but has largely not been found, which is itself informative rather than a mere detection gap, since an impact of the required scale should leave harder-to-erase traces after only ~13,000 years. Genetic evidence is weakly diagnostic with low detectability (0.3). Because substantial primary evidence was in fact reported and searched for by multiple independent geochemistry labs, with mixed/contested replication (some finding elevated spherules, others attributing particles to non-impact sources like fungal spherules or industrial contamination), the ongoing controversy reflects genuine interpretive disagreement over actively studied, fairly detectable strata rather than absence of evidence caused by poor preservation. I set the adjustment at 0.5, between the higher geological/astronomical baseline and the lower material/genetic baseline, since low detectability should not be invoked to fully explain away weak corroboration when the record has already been extensively searched and sampled.
